title: 10.4–10.6 Catch-Up
contentObjective: I can show I am caught up on Lessons 10.4–10.6 by using each lesson's big idea in mixed practice.
languageObjective: I can explain which lesson's big idea I used and how, using key vocabulary from Lessons 10.4–10.6.

vocabulary.definition: Coming up with different, and sometimes unique, solutions to problems.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Idear soluciones diferentes, y a veces únicas, a los problemas.
vocabulary.example: Making the front wheel huge so one pedal push carries you farther.

vocabulary.definition: One full turn of a wheel, gear, or pedal all the way around.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una vuelta completa de una rueda, un engranaje o un pedal.
vocabulary.example: On the Penny Farthing, one pedal rotation makes one wheel rotation.

vocabulary.definition: A toothed wheel that passes motion to another toothed wheel through a chain.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una rueda con dientes que transmite el movimiento a otra rueda con dientes por medio de una cadena.
vocabulary.example: The pedal gear has 48 teeth; the smallest rear gear has 12.

vocabulary.definition: A comparison of two quantities, like pedal rotations to wheel rotations.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una comparación de dos cantidades, como rotaciones del pedal y rotaciones de la rueda.
vocabulary.example: The Penny Farthing's pedal-to-wheel ratio is 1 to 1.

vocabulary.definition: Ratios that make the same comparison using different numbers.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Razones que hacen la misma comparación con números diferentes.
vocabulary.example: 1 rotation per 32 teeth is equivalent to 1.5 rotations per 48 teeth.

vocabulary.definition: The same object, shape, or form repeated multiple times.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El mismo objeto, figura o forma repetido varias veces.
vocabulary.example: A row of identical squares across a tiled wall.

vocabulary.definition: A set of objects or shapes that are repeated and arranged in a regular order.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un conjunto de objetos o figuras que se repiten y se organizan en un orden regular.
vocabulary.example: Circle, square, triangle — circle, square, triangle — again and again.

vocabulary.definition: The smallest chunk of a pattern that repeats.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La parte más pequeña de un patrón que se repite.
vocabulary.example: In circle-square-triangle repeated, the pattern unit is those three shapes.

vocabulary.definition: The story of your relationship with math — and how it has changed over time.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La historia de tu relación con las matemáticas y cómo ha cambiado con el tiempo.
vocabulary.example: In September I dreaded fractions; in June I divide them without fear.

launch.narrative: Missed a lesson — or just want a refresher? This catch-up station reviews Lessons 10.4–10.6: 10.4 Math is Ingenuity, 10.5 Math is Boundless, 10.6 Math is Mine. Read the Big Ideas, warm up with the review problem, then prove you're caught up in the mixed practice.

conceptIntro.heading: The Big Ideas — Lessons 10.4–10.6
conceptIntro.intro: Here is the one thing to remember from each lesson, plus a quick guided example. If one of these feels shaky, that lesson is right above this one in the menu — you can open it any time.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: 10.4: With each pedal rotation, the bicycle travels the length of the perimeter of the wheel. The front wheel is large so the bicycle travels a greater distance with one pedal rotation. • 10.5: Math can be used to create beautiful designs. These designs often have repetition, patterns, and rhythm — and the pattern unit lets you predict what comes next. • 10.6: We are all doers of math and use math in our daily lives. Our math stories continue to grow and evolve as we grow and advance.

iDo.title: The Big Ideas (one per lesson)
lines: Lesson 10.4 — Math is Ingenuity: With each pedal rotation, the bicycle travels the length of the perimeter of the wheel. The front wheel is large so the bicycle travels a greater distance with one pedal rotation.
Lesson 10.5 — Math is Boundless: Math can be used to create beautiful designs. These designs often have repetition, patterns, and rhythm — and the pattern unit lets you predict what comes next.
Lesson 10.6 — Math is Mine: We are all doers of math and use math in our daily lives. Our math stories continue to grow and evolve as we grow and advance.

youDo.title: Show you're caught up
lines: The practice below mixes problems from Lessons 10.4–10.6. Each problem is tagged with its lesson number.
Stuck on one lesson's problems? Open that lesson from the curriculum menu for the full re-teach.

explore.label: Then and now: when did this become part of your math story? Sort them.
categories: I could already do this in September
I learned or grew into this during Grade 6

cards.text: Estimate how many people fit on a Ferris wheel
Divide a fraction by a fraction
Use ratios and unit rates to compare deals
Find a percent of a number
Split a bill so everyone pays a fair share
Plot points in all four quadrants of the coordinate plane

explore.instructions: The September cards come straight from Lesson 1-1 — you were already a doer of math before this year started. The Grade 6 cards are what this year added. After sorting, tell a partner which new skill you have actually used outside of class.

connect.scenario: You and your classmates each wrote about your math stories at the beginning of the school year. Everyone has their own math story, and as you encounter new challenges and experiences, your story might change.
connect.promptQuestion: How does your classmate's end-of-school-year math story compare to your story?
connect.prompt: Describe how your math story has ___ this year, ask a ___ about their story, and then ___ the two to see how they are alike and different.

check.stem: In September you estimated the Ferris wheel as 20 cars × 4 riders = about 80. Which of these uses a tool you did NOT have in September to extend that same estimate?
choices: Multiplying the 80 riders per turn by 6 turns per hour to find a rate of 480 riders per hour
Adding the 20 cars and 4 riders together to get 24
Guessing a completely different, unrelated number
Deciding not to estimate the Ferris wheel at all
check.explanation: 80 × 6 = 480 uses a rate, a tool this year's math added — the September estimate of 20 × 4 could not do this. Adding 20 + 4 or guessing does not use any new math tool at all.

check.stem: Which statement best distinguishes a real comparison of math stories with a classmate from just repeating what you already believe?
choices: Naming something the classmate actually said, plus one genuine similarity AND one genuine difference between the two stories
Writing 'we both got better at math' and stopping there
Copying your own September answer word for word
Skipping the classmate entirely and writing only about yourself
check.explanation: The lesson's check requires reporting something the classmate actually said and naming a genuine similarity and a genuine difference — a vague claim like 'we both got better' does not show that any real conversation happened.

check.stem: A student writes, 'My classmate's story changed the same way mine did — we both feel more confident now.' What is missing from this comparison?
choices: A genuine DIFFERENCE between the two stories, not just a shared similarity
The classmate's full name and grade
The exact date Lesson 1-1 was taught
A drawing of the Ferris wheel
check.explanation: A complete comparison names both a similarity and a difference; this answer only states a similarity, so it does not meet the lesson's check for a complete answer.

connect.modelAnswer: My classmate said that in September he only felt safe in math when he could copy an example, and now he tries problems first and checks the example after. We both got more comfortable being wrong on a first try. But our stories differ: his confidence grew most in equations, while mine grew most in ratios, because I started using unit rates when I shop with my mom.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 10.4) On the Penny Farthing, what is the ratio of pedal rotations to front-wheel rotations?
approaching.explanation: The pedals are attached directly to the front wheel, so each pedal rotation rotates the wheel one time — a 1 to 1 ratio.
choiceFeedback: 1 to 2 would mean each pedal rotation turns the wheel twice, but the pedals are attached directly to the wheel.
2 to 1 would mean the rider must pedal twice for one wheel turn, but one pedal rotation gives one wheel rotation.
1 to 4 describes the chain bike's smallest gear, not the Penny Farthing.
hints: The pedals are attached directly to the front wheel.
One pedal rotation makes the wheel turn how many times?
Each pedal rotation rotates the wheel one time.
approaching.stemEs: (Lección 10.4) En la Penny Farthing, ¿cuál es la razón de rotaciones del pedal a rotaciones de la rueda delantera?
approaching.explanationEs: Los pedales están conectados directamente a la rueda delantera, así que cada rotación del pedal gira la rueda una vez — una razón de 1 a 1.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 10.4) How far does the Penny Farthing travel with each pedal rotation?
choices: The length of the perimeter of the front wheel
It does not move a fixed distance
approaching.explanation: One wheel rotation rolls the bike forward exactly the perimeter of the wheel, and one pedal rotation makes one wheel rotation.
choiceFeedback: The rider's height does not determine rolling distance — the wheel's perimeter does.
The pedal's length changes how hard you have to push, not how far the wheel rolls in one turn.
It does move a fixed distance — one full roll of the wheel is always the same length.
hints: Picture the wheel rolling one full turn on the ground.
The distance it covers is the distance all the way around the wheel.
That distance around the wheel is its perimeter.
approaching.stemEs: (Lección 10.4) ¿Qué distancia recorre la bicicleta Penny Farthing con cada rotación del pedal?
approaching.explanationEs: Una rotación de la rueda hace avanzar la bicicleta exactamente el perímetro de la rueda, y una rotación del pedal produce una rotación de la rueda.
choicesEs: La longitud del perímetro de la rueda delantera

approaching.stem: (Lesson 10.5) In geometric design, what is repetition?
choices: The same object or shape repeated multiple times
A set of different shapes arranged randomly
Shapes that vary in size and order of appearance
approaching.explanation: Repetition involves one repeated object, shape, or form — and because of that, it has predictability.
choiceFeedback: A random arrangement has no rule, so it is neither repetition nor a pattern.
Varying size and order describes rhythm, not repetition.
Color alone does not make a design element — repetition is about a repeated shape.
hints: The word itself is a clue: something repeats.
How many different objects does repetition involve?
One object or shape, repeated multiple times.
approaching.stemEs: (Lección 10.5) En el diseño geométrico, ¿qué es la repetición?
approaching.explanationEs: La repetición usa un objeto, figura o forma repetido — y por eso es predecible.
choicesEs: El mismo objeto o figura repetido varias veces
Un conjunto de figuras distintas colocadas al azar
Figuras que varían en tamaño y en orden de aparición

approaching.stem: (Lesson 10.5) A border shows: pink circle, purple square, blue triangle, pink circle, purple square, blue triangle. What are the next three shapes?
choices: Pink circle, purple square, blue triangle
Blue triangle, purple square, pink circle
Pink circle, blue triangle, purple square
approaching.explanation: The pattern unit is circle, square, triangle, so it repeats in the same order: a pink circle, a purple square, and a blue triangle.
choiceFeedback: That reverses the unit — a pattern repeats in the SAME order, not backwards.
That swaps the square and triangle; the unit's order never changes.
A pattern has predictability — that is exactly what makes it a pattern.
hints: Find the chunk that repeats.
The unit is circle, square, triangle.
After a triangle, the unit starts over.
approaching.stemEs: (Lección 10.5) Un borde muestra: círculo rosado, cuadrado morado, triángulo azul, círculo rosado, cuadrado morado, triángulo azul. ¿Cuáles son las siguientes tres figuras?
approaching.explanationEs: La unidad del patrón es círculo, cuadrado, triángulo, así que se repite en el mismo orden: un círculo rosado, un cuadrado morado y un triángulo azul.
choicesEs: Círculo rosado, cuadrado morado, triángulo azul
Triángulo azul, cuadrado morado, círculo rosado
Círculo rosado, triángulo azul, cuadrado morado

approaching.stem: (Lesson 10.6) In Lesson 1-1 you estimated the Ferris wheel: 20 cars each holding about 4 people. About how many riders was that?
approaching.explanation: 20 × 4 = 80 — the same estimate you made in September, and it still holds up.
choiceFeedback: That adds 20 + 4 instead of multiplying.
That divides 20 by 4 instead of multiplying.
That multiplies as if each car held 20 people.
hints: This is the very first estimate of the year — 20 groups of 4.
Multiply the cars by the riders per car.
approaching.stemEs: (Lección 10.6) En la Lección 1-1 estimaste la rueda de la fortuna: 20 cabinas con unas 4 personas cada una. ¿Aproximadamente cuántos pasajeros eran?
approaching.explanationEs: 20 × 4 = 80 — la misma estimación que hiciste en septiembre, y sigue siendo válida.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 10.6) How has your attitude about math changed over the year?
approaching.modelAnswer: In September I thought being good at math meant being fast. Now I think it means sticking with a problem — some of my best work this year came on the second or third try.
sentenceStems: In September I thought math was ___ .
approaching.stemEs: (Lección 10.6) ¿Cómo ha cambiado tu actitud hacia las matemáticas durante el año?

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 10.4) The pedal gear turns 48 teeth per rotation. The largest rear gear needs 32 teeth for one full rotation. How many rotations does the rear wheel make for each pedal rotation?
onLevel.explanation: 48 ÷ 32 = 1.5, so the rear wheel makes 1.5 rotations for each pedal rotation.
choiceFeedback: That subtracts 48 − 32 instead of dividing 48 by 32.
That divides 32 by 48 the wrong way around — the wheel turns MORE than once, not less.
2 rotations would need a 24-tooth gear, since 48 ÷ 24 = 2.
hints: The chain delivers 48 teeth of motion; the gear uses 32 per rotation.
How many groups of 32 fit in 48?
Divide 48 by 32.
onLevel.stemEs: (Lección 10.4) El engranaje del pedal mueve 48 dientes por rotación. El engranaje trasero más grande necesita 32 dientes para una rotación completa. ¿Cuántas rotaciones da la rueda trasera por cada rotación del pedal?
onLevel.explanationEs: 48 ÷ 32 = 1.5, así que la rueda trasera da 1.5 rotaciones por cada rotación del pedal.

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 10.4) The smallest rear gear has 12 teeth. How many rotations will the rear wheel make for each rotation of the 48-tooth pedal gear?
onLevel.explanation: 48 ÷ 12 = 4, so the rear wheel makes 4 rotations for each pedal rotation.
choiceFeedback: That subtracts 48 − 12 instead of dividing 48 by 12.
3 rotations would need a 16-tooth gear, since 48 ÷ 16 = 3.
That divides 12 by 48 the wrong way around — the small gear turns MORE than the pedal gear, not less.
hints: The chain delivers 48 teeth of motion; this gear uses only 12 per rotation.
How many groups of 12 fit in 48?
Divide 48 by 12.
onLevel.stemEs: (Lección 10.4) El engranaje trasero más pequeño tiene 12 dientes. ¿Cuántas rotaciones dará la rueda trasera por cada rotación del engranaje de pedal de 48 dientes?
onLevel.explanationEs: 48 ÷ 12 = 4, así que la rueda trasera da 4 rotaciones por cada rotación del pedal.

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 10.5) The pattern unit circle-square-triangle repeats. What is shape number 12?
onLevel.explanation: 12 ÷ 3 = 4 with no remainder, so shape 12 ends a complete unit — the triangle, which is the last shape of the unit.
choiceFeedback: The circle is position 1 of a unit — that would need a remainder of 1, but 12 ÷ 3 has remainder 0.
The square is position 2 of a unit — that would need a remainder of 2, but 12 ÷ 3 has remainder 0.
It CAN be determined — a pattern's predictability is the point of the pattern unit.
hints: The unit is 3 shapes long. Divide 12 by 3.
12 ÷ 3 = 4 exactly, remainder 0.
No remainder means the LAST shape of the unit.
onLevel.stemEs: (Lección 10.5) La unidad del patrón círculo-cuadrado-triángulo se repite. ¿Cuál es la figura número 12?
onLevel.explanationEs: 12 ÷ 3 = 4 sin residuo, así que la figura 12 termina una unidad completa — el triángulo, que es la última figura de la unidad.

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 10.5) Same pattern. What is shape number 20?
choices: The 20th shape starts a new pattern
onLevel.explanation: 20 ÷ 3 = 6 remainder 2 (since 6 × 3 = 18 and 20 − 18 = 2), and the second shape in the unit is the purple square.
choiceFeedback: The circle needs a remainder of 1, but 20 − 18 = 2.
The triangle needs a remainder of 0, but 20 ÷ 3 leaves a remainder of 2.
The pattern never changes its unit — position 20 is still inside the same repeating pattern.
hints: How many complete units of 3 fit in 20?
6 units use 18 shapes; 20 − 18 = 2 left over.
Count 2 into the unit: circle, then ___ .
onLevel.stemEs: (Lección 10.5) El mismo patrón. ¿Cuál es la figura número 20?
onLevel.explanationEs: 20 ÷ 3 = 6 con residuo 2 (porque 6 × 3 = 18 y 20 − 18 = 2), y la segunda figura de la unidad es el cuadrado morado.
choicesEs: La figura 20 comienza un patrón nuevo

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 10.6) Now stretch the September estimate with this year's math: about 80 riders per turn, 6 turns each hour. About how many riders per hour?
onLevel.explanation: 80 riders on each of 6 turns is 80 × 6 = 480 riders per hour — a rate, one of this year's tools.
choiceFeedback: That adds 80 + 6 instead of multiplying.
That divides 80 by 6 instead of multiplying.
That multiplies by 10 instead of 6.
hints: Each turn carries a full load of about 80.
There are 6 turns in an hour.
onLevel.stemEs: (Lección 10.6) Ahora amplía la estimación de septiembre con las matemáticas de este año: unos 80 pasajeros por vuelta, 6 vueltas por hora. ¿Aproximadamente cuántos pasajeros por hora?
onLevel.explanationEs: 80 pasajeros en cada una de 6 vueltas es 80 × 6 = 480 pasajeros por hora — una tasa, una de las herramientas de este año.

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 10.6) Percents were new this year. What is 50% of 157?
onLevel.explanation: 50% means half, and 157 ÷ 2 = 78.5 — the very number you decomposed back in Lesson 1-1.
choiceFeedback: 77.5 is half of 155, not 157.
107 subtracts 50 from 157 instead of taking 50 percent.
hints: 50% of a number is half of it.
Half of 157 means 157 ÷ 2.
Check your answer by doubling it — you should land back on 157.
onLevel.stemEs: (Lección 10.6) Los porcentajes fueron nuevos este año. ¿Cuánto es el 50% de 157?
onLevel.explanationEs: 50% significa la mitad, y 157 ÷ 2 = 78.5 — el mismo número que descompusiste en la Lección 1-1.

extending.stem: (Lesson 10.4) The rider makes 3 full pedal rotations with the chain on the 32-tooth gear. How many rotations does the rear wheel make?
extending.explanation: Three pedal rotations move 3 × 48 = 144 teeth of chain, and 144 ÷ 32 = 4.5 rear-wheel rotations.
choiceFeedback: 3 rotations forgets the gear ratio — the wheel turns 1.5 times for EACH pedal rotation, not once.
96 is 3 × 32, which multiplies by the gear's teeth instead of finding rotations.
6 uses a ratio of 2 rotations per pedal, but 48 ÷ 32 = 1.5, not 2.
hints: Each pedal rotation gives 48 ÷ 32 = 1.5 wheel rotations.
You have 3 pedal rotations.
Multiply 3 × 1.5.
extending.stemEs: (Lección 10.4) El ciclista da 3 rotaciones completas del pedal con la cadena en el engranaje de 32 dientes. ¿Cuántas rotaciones da la rueda trasera?
extending.explanationEs: Tres rotaciones del pedal mueven 3 × 48 = 144 dientes de cadena, y 144 ÷ 32 = 4.5 rotaciones de la rueda trasera.

extending.stem: (Lesson 10.5) The circle-square-triangle pattern continues. What is shape number 25?
extending.explanation: 25 ÷ 3 = 8 remainder 1 (since 8 × 3 = 24 and 25 − 24 = 1), and the first shape of the unit is the pink circle.
choiceFeedback: The square needs a remainder of 2, but 25 − 24 = 1.
The triangle needs a remainder of 0, but 25 ÷ 3 leaves a remainder of 1.
A pattern is boundless — it continues, so shape 25 exists and is predictable.
hints: How many complete units of 3 fit in 25?
8 units use 24 shapes; 25 − 24 = 1 left over.
A remainder of 1 means the FIRST shape of the unit.
extending.stemEs: (Lección 10.5) El patrón círculo-cuadrado-triángulo continúa. ¿Cuál es la figura número 25?
extending.explanationEs: 25 ÷ 3 = 8 con residuo 1 (porque 8 × 3 = 24 y 25 − 24 = 1), y la primera figura de la unidad es el círculo rosado.

extending.stem: (Lesson 10.6) Which set shows THREE correct ways to write 78.5 using skills from this year?
extending.explanation: All three rebuild 78.5 exactly: 157 ÷ 2 = 78.5, 50% of 157 = 78.5, and 78½ = 78.5.
choiceFeedback: 78¼ = 78.25, so that set contains an error.
156 ÷ 2 = 78, so that set contains an error.
25% of 157 = 39.25, so that set contains an error.
hints: Check every member of each set against 78.5.
One wrong member spoils the whole set.
Find the set where all three land exactly on 78.5.
extending.stemEs: (Lección 10.6) ¿Cuál conjunto muestra TRES maneras correctas de escribir 78.5 usando destrezas de este año?
extending.explanationEs: Las tres reconstruyen 78.5 exactamente: 157 ÷ 2 = 78.5, 50% de 157 = 78.5, y 78½ = 78.5.

practice.commonMistake: Treating your math story as finished — writing the same answers you wrote in Lesson 1-1 instead of looking for what actually changed. The story grows and evolves; a retrospective that copies September has missed the point.

optionalActivity.name: Catch-Up Challenge
optionalActivity.intro: Mix it up: pick the right lesson's big idea for each problem — that's the real catch-up skill.

exitTicket.stem: (Catch-up check, from Lesson 10.5) Which statement best matches this lesson's summary of 'Math is Boundless'?
choices: Math can be used to create beautiful designs, which often have repetition, patterns, and rhythm
Designs only count as mathematical if they are perfectly predictable
Rhythm is the only real element of design
exitTicket.explanation: The summary names all three elements — repetition, patterns, and rhythm — as the ways math creates beautiful, endless designs.
hints: Look back at the Summarize slide.
It names three elements of design.
Which option includes all three?

parallelPractice.stem: (Lesson 10.4) A new model has 2 blue tiles for every 3 gold tiles. Write the ratio blue:gold.

steps.promptEs: Escribe primero azul y luego dorado: ___.

hints: Re-read the question. What exactly is it asking you to find?
Use the visual model, then complete one step at a time.
Start like this: Blue tiles: 2.
parallelPractice.explanation: Blue tiles: 2. Gold tiles: 3. Write blue first, then gold: 2:3.
parallelPractice.stemEs: Un nuevo modelo tiene 2 fichas azules por cada 3 fichas doradas. Escribe la razón azul:dorado.
hintsEs: Vuelve a leer la pregunta. ¿Qué te pide encontrar exactamente?
Usa el modelo visual y completa un paso a la vez.
Empieza así: Fichas azules: 2.
parallelPractice.explanationEs: Fichas azules: 2. Fichas doradas: 3. Escribe primero azul y luego dorado: 2:3.

Start like this: Blue tiles: 4.

parallelPractice.stem: (Lesson 10.5) Divide 252 by 6. Give the quotient and remainder.
hints: Re-read the question. What exactly is it asking you to find?
Use the visual model, then complete one step at a time.
Start like this: 6 fits into 252 about 42 times.
parallelPractice.explanation: 6 fits into 252 about 42 times. Multiply back: 6 × 42 = 252. The amount left is 0.
parallelPractice.stemEs: Divide 252 entre 6. Escribe el cociente y el residuo.
hintsEs: Vuelve a leer la pregunta. ¿Qué te pide encontrar exactamente?
Usa el modelo visual y completa un paso a la vez.
Empieza así: 6 cabe en 252 aproximadamente 42 veces.
parallelPractice.explanationEs: 6 cabe en 252 aproximadamente 42 veces. Multiplica para comprobar: 6 × 42 = 252. La cantidad que sobra es 0.

parallelPractice.stem: (Lesson 10.5) Divide 316 by 7. Give the quotient and remainder.
hints: Re-read the question. What exactly is it asking you to find?
Use the visual model, then complete one step at a time.
Start like this: 7 fits into 316 about 45 times.
parallelPractice.explanation: 7 fits into 316 about 45 times. Multiply back: 7 × 45 = 315. The amount left is 1.
parallelPractice.stemEs: Divide 316 entre 7. Escribe el cociente y el residuo.
hintsEs: Vuelve a leer la pregunta. ¿Qué te pide encontrar exactamente?
Usa el modelo visual y completa un paso a la vez.
Empieza así: 7 cabe en 316 aproximadamente 45 veces.
parallelPractice.explanationEs: 7 cabe en 316 aproximadamente 45 veces. Multiplica para comprobar: 7 × 45 = 315. La cantidad que sobra es 1.

parallelPractice.stem: (Lesson 10.5) Divide 386 by 8. Give the quotient and remainder.
hints: Re-read the question. What exactly is it asking you to find?
